extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and their practitioners (agents/attorneys); USPTO staff referencing filing rules
extracted.subtask_short: filing and completion of patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for obtaining a filing date and completing U.S. patent applications (nonprovisional, provisional, continuation/divisional/CPA), including fees, oath/declaration timing, conversion rules, and post-filing restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date entitlement for nonprovisional applications filed on or after Dec 18, 2013
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for design applications, the filing date is the date on which a specification, with or without claims, is received by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design applications (except CPA) require a specification including at least one claim and any required drawings to obtain a filing date. Although minimal formal requirements were reduced by PLTIA, applicants are advised that including claims on filing is a best practice to ensure disclosure satisfies 35 U.S.C. 112(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date entitlement for nonprovisional applications filed before Dec 18, 2013
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed prior to Dec 18, 2013, a filing date is the date a specification containing a description (37 CFR 1.71), at least one claim (37 CFR 1.75), and any required drawings (37 CFR 1.81(a)) are filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to meet these requirements will result in denial of a filing date; the filing date becomes the date when all requirements are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date entitlement for provisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date of a provisional application is the date a specification as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112(a) and any drawing required by 37 CFR 1.81(a) are filed. A provisional must include the cover sheet required by 37 CFR 1.51(c)(1) (or an ADS) or it will be treated as a nonprovisional under paragraph (b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A provisional may not be amended after the filing date except to make it comply with statute/regulations. Provisional applications become abandoned no later than 12 months after their filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: No new matter after filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Any claim or drawing submitted after the filing date of an application may not contain new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments (including submission of claims and drawings) after filing cannot introduce subject matter that would have been new matter in the original application. This applies regardless of whether claims/drawings are submitted after a minimal filing-date entitlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation/divisional/continuation-in-part filing allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuing application may be filed as a continuation, divisional, or continuation-in-part under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, or 365(c) and 37 CFR 1.78(c) and (d); specific subparagraphs of 37 CFR 1.53 specify which type must be filed under which paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuation-in-part applications (which can disclose/claim subject matter not disclosed in the prior application) or any continuation/divisional that names an inventor not named in the prior application must be filed under paragraph (b). Continuations or divisionals that name the same or fewer inventors may be filed under paragraph (d) when appropriate (e.g., design CPA rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued prosecution application (CPA) requirements and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A CPA is a nonprovisional application that must be filed on or after Dec 1, 1997 and applies only to design applications; only a continuation or divisional (not a continuation-in-part) may be filed as a CPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CPA practice: prior nonprovisional must be complete as defined by 37 CFR 1.51(b) (except possibly the oath if CPA filed on/after Sept 16, 2012) and must contain an ADS indicating inventor info. CPA filing fee/search/exam fees per 37 CFR 1.16 apply. A CPA may be filed by fewer than all inventors if accompanied by a statement requesting deletion of named persons who are not inventors; no person may be named as an inventor in the CPA who was not named in the prior application except by correction under 37 CFR 1.48. Any new change in a CPA must be by amendment to the prior application as it existed immediately prior to filing the CPA; no amendment may introduce new matter. Any new specification filed with the CPA request is treated as a substitute specification under 37 CFR 1.125 (not part of the original papers). Filing a CPA waives confidentiality under 35 U.S.C. 122 to the extent members of the public entitled to access to either application may receive similar access to others in the file jacket. A CPA must include the specific reference required by 35 U.S.C. 120 and that specific reference may not be deleted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion of nonprovisional application missing fees/claims/oath (with correspondence address)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application accorded a filing date lacks the basic filing fee, search fee, examination fee, at least one claim, or the inventor's oath/declaration and a correspondence address has been provided, the applicant will be notified and given a period of time to submit the missing items to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will send a Notice to File Missing Parts; for applications filed on/after Sept 16, 2012, the inventor's oath/declaration may be postponed subject to conditions (see separate criterion). Payment of required fees and any surcharge (37 CFR 1.16(f)) must be made within the time set in the notice. If the surcharge is not paid on filing, the Office will require it later; payment of the surcharge cannot be postponed to Notice of Allowance or issue fee payment unless conditions for postponement are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion of nonprovisional application missing fees/claims/oath (without correspondence address)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application has no correspondence address and is missing required fees, claims, or oath/declaration, applicant generally has a fixed short period from the filing date to supply missing parts (e.g., three months) to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific timeframes vary by rule and filing-date regime (e.g., some pre- and post-AIA rules described two months or three months). If applicant fails to correct within the time period or timely petition, proceedings will be terminated and fees refunded less handling fee per 37 CFR 1.21(n).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor's oath or declaration timing and postponement conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor's oath or declaration required by 37 CFR 1.63 (or substitute statement under 1.64) must be filed within the time specified by 37 CFR 1.53(f)(1) or (f)(2), except it may be postponed until the application is otherwise in condition for allowance if certain conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications filed on or after Sept 16, 2012, an oath or substitute statement must be filed no later than the date the issue fee is paid to avoid abandonment; this period is not extendable under 37 CFR 1.136. Conditions enabling postponement include the application being an original (non-reissue) application and containing an ADS (37 CFR 1.76) identifying each inventor by legal name and mailing/residence address. If the oath/declaration is not submitted on filing, a surcharge under 37 CFR 1.16(f) is required; payment of this surcharge cannot be postponed beyond the missing-parts period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess claims, multiple dependent claim, and application size fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Excess claims fees (37 CFR 1.16(h),(i)), the multiple dependent claim fee (1.16(j)), and any application size fee (1.16(s)) must be paid when due or the claims canceled by amendment prior to the expiration of the time period set for reply in any notice of fee deficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If these fees are not timely paid, the Office will require payment or cancellation to avoid abandonment. Fees related to amendments necessitating application size fees must be paid prior to the expiration of the reply period set in the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion between provisional and nonprovisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application may be converted to a nonprovisional application (and vice versa in limited circumstances); conversion must be filed before the earliest of abandonment, payment of the issue fee, or expiration of 12 months from the provisional filing date (where applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion requires payment of applicable fees (processing fee 37 CFR 1.17(q) or 1.17(i) as applicable), any required claims (except where provisional already contains at least one claim), and for conversion to nonprovisional the filing/search/examination fees, inventor's oath/declaration, and any surcharge if those items were not present on the provisional filing date. Conversion of a provisional to a nonprovisional will result in the patent term being measured from at least the filing date of the provisional for which conversion is requested; to avoid adverse patent-term impact, applicants should consider filing a nonprovisional claiming benefit under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) instead of converting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications not placed on examination until required parts received
rubrics_metrics.description: An application filed under paragraphs (b) or (d) will not be placed on the files for examination until all required parts, complying with the rules, are received, except minor informalities may be waived subject to later correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: applications filed on or after Sept 16, 2012 may be forwarded for examination even if lacking the inventor's oath/declaration provided a compliant ADS is filed. Provisional applications are not examined and become abandoned after 12 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to meet filing date requirements and remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application deposited under relevant paragraphs does not meet the requirements to be entitled to a filing date, the applicant will be notified (if correspondence address provided) and given time to correct; failure to timely correct or petition results in termination of proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review of a notification that original papers lack portions must be by petition under the applicable paragraph accompanied by the fee in 37 CFR 1.17(f) and must be timely per 37 CFR 1.181(f). If proceedings terminate, application may be disposed of and filing fees refunded less handling fee per 37 CFR 1.21(n). A request for continued examination will be treated instead in some circumstances (e.g., certain design/non-design distinctions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents and formality of CPA request
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to identifying the prior application number, the request for an application under CPA paragraph should furnish, to the best of the applicant's ability, the title of the invention, name of applicant(s), and correspondence address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items help ensure correct assignment of the specific reference and proper handling. See 37 CFR 1.103(b) for requesting limited suspension of action in a CPA-filed application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of application numbers and copy availability
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.53(a) indicates an application number is assigned for identification to any paper purporting to be an application even if incomplete or informal. Copies of applications will be provided by USPTO upon request and payment of the fee under 37 CFR 1.19(b) unless the application has been disposed of.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application disposed of (e.g., due to failure to correct missing parts) may not be available for copying; fees for copies and procedures for requesting are set out in the cited regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings and necessity for understanding the invention
rubrics_metrics.description: If the subject matter admits of illustration by a drawing or a drawing is necessary for understanding the invention, the Office continues to require drawings; any claim or drawing submitted after the filing date may not contain new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should submit drawings on filing if they facilitate understanding; provisional applications filed on or after Dec 18, 2013 may receive a filing date even without drawings, but where drawings are necessary they should nonetheless be filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surcharge payment and deposit-account charging
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a surcharge under 37 CFR 1.16(f) is required (e.g., when claims or oath are not submitted on filing), it must be paid within the missing-parts time period; if a general authorization to charge a deposit account covering 1.16 fees is submitted on filing, the Office will charge the surcharge to the deposit account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment of the surcharge cannot be postponed until Notice of Allowance or issue fee payment unless the statutory/postponement conditions are met.
